title: UGT recipe (draft 5)
description: What a recipe is, for which task, from which source, what a run takes and gives, what stays usable after it, what the user must supply and what access beyond the sandbox it needs. Everything that runs lives in the recipe's compose.yaml. Evidence of verification is not part of a recipe: the catalogue keeps it. Provisional: recipe_format names the draft, and each breaking change before v1 bumps it.

id.description: <owner>/<repo>/<task> in lowercase: the project and the job this recipe does. In the catalogue it matches the folder recipes/<owner>/<repo>/<task>.

commit.description: Full commit SHA the package was built from.

release.description: Release artifact used instead of a source build, when applicable.

task.description: The user's task as an output, in plain words.

x-display.description: Optional catalogue wording for this recipe, distinct from the execution task. Plain text describing only the packaged capability.

summary.description: One short sentence explaining the result, used on cards and in page introductions.

description.description: Optional fuller explanation of useful applications and the packaged scope. Plain text; separate paragraphs with a blank line. Keep settings, requirements, permissions and limitations in their structured fields.

x-licences.description: Original licence or model-notice sources for the packaged components. Supplements, never replaces, the complete licence notice. Use immutable source links where available.

x-job.description: The catalogue's job this recipe does, as an id from spec/catalogue/v0/jobs.json, such as remove-vocals. The catalogue groups and names recipes by it; ugt itself ignores it.

kind.description: job: the task service runs to completion on the user's inputs and writes outputs/; nothing keeps running. service: the stack keeps running for the user, and has no task service: up starts it and its check proves it works.

provides.description: What stays usable after a run. Only a service provides pages and endpoints: UGT publishes each port named here on 127.0.0.1, at an address that stays the same, so compose.yaml does not publish it. A command's service has profiles: [command] and an MCP server's profiles: [mcp], so each runs only when used.

pages.description: What a person opens in the browser.

commands.description: What the user types in their terminal. Each runs its service with the user's arguments, in the folder they run it in.

mcp_servers.description: MCP servers whose tools UGT serves among its own, in every AI app connected to it. Each runs its service, which speaks MCP over stdin and stdout.

adapted_from.description: Permanent URL of the Compose file this recipe was adopted from (at a pinned commit), so it can be re-imported when upstream changes.

settings.description: What the user must supply. Each becomes ${NAME} in compose.yaml; the executor fills it, keeping secrets in the system keychain.

name.description: An upper-case environment variable name; UGT_, COMPOSE_ and DOCKER_ names belong to the executor.

access.description: Each kind of access beyond the sandbox the recipe needs, with why. ugt reads what compose.yaml really grants from Compose's resolved model and refuses a recipe whose grants and declarations differ; the user agrees to the declared access before it runs. internet: a running service reaches the internet. lan: a port published beyond 127.0.0.1. host-services: extra_hosts pointing at host-gateway. host-folder: a bind mount outside ./inputs, ./outputs and ./recipe, or a volume bound to a host path. engine: the container engine's socket, or containers, volumes and networks outside the recipe. ssh-agent: a build given the user's SSH agent. device: host devices. capabilities: cap_add. privileged: privileged, an unconfined security profile, or a build's host network or entitlements. host-namespace: the host's network, process, IPC, UTS, user or cgroup namespace.

why.description: Why the recipe needs it, in plain words the user reads before agreeing.

inputs.description: What a run takes from the user.

outputs.description: What a job's run delivers to the user. A job without outputs only provides commands or MCP servers.

licence.description: SPDX identifier of the upstream project, plus a note if it affects sharing or hosting.

what.description: What the user gets, in plain words they read when it is ready.

port.description: The port the service listens on, inside its container.

path.description: Where it starts; / when not given.

port.description: The port the service listens on, inside its container.

path.description: Where it starts; / when not given.

protocol.description: How software reaches it, as a URL scheme such as postgresql or redis; http when not given.

path.description: Workspace-relative path under inputs/ or outputs/.
